beats.care: Carry earphones. The fine is up to ₹1,000, and ignoring staff can mean up to ₹5,000 or six months' jail.
beats.what: Western and Central Railway staff will ask people playing phone audio without earphones to stop, and can fine those who don't.
beats.why: Commuters complain loud audio in crowded peak-hour coaches is annoying and sometimes sparks arguments, a passenger group says.

cards.body: Under Section 145 of the Railways Act, continuing after staff tell you to stop can bring this fine, six months' simple jail, or both.
cards.caption: maximum fine if you keep going after a warning

cards.body: A Western Railway official said offenders 'will first be warned', then fined. Railways may play announcements in Marathi, Hindi and English.
cards.title: How it will work

opts: You get a warning to stop
cards.q: What happens first if staff catch you playing audio loudly?
cards.why: Officials say people will be warned first; fines come if they keep going.

cards.q: Loud reels on the local are…

cards.body: It's not just trains: BEST has started putting up stickers in its buses asking people not to play loud audio on phones.

cover.label: fine for loud phone audio on trains

hook: Could *playing reels out loud* on a local cost you money?

learn.t: Railway rules on loud calls and offensive ringtones date back to Railway Board guidelines from July 2012.
